claims.text: The investigated nanoparticles are composed of Au, Co, Cu, Ni, and Pt.
AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will exhibit enhanced high-temperature thermal stability compared with traditional alloys.
The atomic arrangement and bonding within the nanoparticles mediate their response to high-temperature exposure.
The multicomponent composition and atomic arrangement of high-entropy alloys increase configurational entropy.
Increased configurational entropy contributes to the thermal stability of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Under identical high-temperature conditions, AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will retain greater structural integrity than alloy nanoparticles containing fewer than five metals.
Under identical high-temperature conditions, AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will undergo less thermal degradation than alloy nanoparticles containing fewer than five metals.
The actual high-temperature thermal stability of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles has not been experimentally validated.
